sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Abies alba is a large evergreen conifer of European mountains, usually 45–50 m tall and sometimes taller. Its flattened, blunt needles often lie in two comb-like rows and have two pale bands beneath. Upright cones mature on the branches and disintegrate there, leaving the central axis. It grows mainly in cool, moist mountain climates; its timber is used in construction and joinery.

sections.title: Related firs
sections.text: Like Abies nordmanniana, this fir has upright cones that break apart on the tree. A. alba is native to Europe, while A. nordmanniana is native farther east, from the Caucasus and northern Türkiye.
